chapter: Washington in the 1930s: big bands, lessons, first jobs
title: The idea of genius and the hunchbacked pianist Toby Walker
summary: He meets the word genius, and describes Toby Walker, a Washington pianist who died at twenty-five.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: But in the meantime, in listening to the local pianists around, and by this time I'm beginning to move around and sneak into the club every now and then, hearing different people and hearing people talk about other musicians. I think I must have come in contact with what people call this word "genius." I never realized what that word really meant. And as a matter of fact, I didn't realize that that's what Art Tatum was. I think they were geniuses. That's a relative term. I guess it's up to the way you see the thing.

Anyway, there was a local fellow in Washington here, he was a young man -- I guess he must have been around 18 or 19. His name was Toby Walker. He was a hunchback, and he'd kind of sit sideways at the piano. He just fantastic things on the piano, beyond... I thought this fellow James Morgan that I mentioned before was great, which he really was. But this guy Toby Walker was just beyond anything I had heard in person. Unfortunately, he died when he was 25 years old. And later, I really got to meet him and know him and become friends with him. And I'll talk more about him later.
But in all of the time I feel that I'm growing as a
musician. I'm learning, and I don't think there was a day since that piano was sitting in my home that I didn't play it, every chance I got, that one or any other piano.
